transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I, um… I came in because I’m really not sleeping. Since that warehouse inspection, I just lie there and my mind keeps replaying little pieces of it, like it won’t shut off. I used to be able to sleep pretty normally, even when work was stressful—insurance stuff can be boring but also weirdly intense, you know, all the forms and site notes and people arguing over wording…

But now when I finally do drift off, I wake up sweaty and wide awake, like I’m right back near that blast again. It’s been really hard to function.
Can you tell me more about what happened during the warehouse inspection? Were there any events that felt scary, dangerous, or threatening to you or others at that time?

I… I don’t know how to explain it clearly. It was supposed to be routine, like walk-through, notes, photos, checking conditions, that kind of thing. Warehouses all have that same smell too, cardboard and dust and like… machine oil, I guess. I remember thinking I should’ve worn different shoes because the floor was uneven and I was annoyed about that, which feels stupid to remember.

And then—sorry, I’m kind of losing the thread. There was the blast, or whatever happened, and everyone kind of reacted all at once. It felt dangerous, yeah. I don’t know exactly what caused it. I keep second-guessing what I saw versus what I think I saw. But in the moment it felt like something was really wrong and people could get hurt.
Since the warehouse incident, have you had any moments where you feel like you're back there again, like the event is reoccurring in some way, even when you know you're safe?

Yeah… kind of. Not like I fully think I’m there, exactly, but during the day I’ll be doing something normal, like reviewing a policy or a loss report, and then out of nowhere I get this really sharp image of the worker on the floor, and the air looking all sooty.

And it’s strange because I can be sitting at my desk with my coffee and my spreadsheets—well, not spreadsheets exactly, more the claim notes, but still—and my body reacts before I even catch up. Like I tense up and everything just drops for a second, like I’m back in that moment.
Since the warehouse incident, have you noticed yourself avoiding certain places, people, or activities that remind you of what happened?

Yeah… I mean, I didn’t think of it as avoiding at first. I kept telling myself I was just “busy,” because there’s always a pile of work anyway, and people act like insurance is just paperwork but the phone never stops, honestly.

But… yes. I’ve been avoiding the warehouse file. I leave it sitting there, and if an email comes in about it—or even sometimes about similar industrial accounts—I just kind of freeze. Opening it makes my stomach drop. And I’ve let calls go to voicemail when I can tell they’re about that kind of account, which I know isn’t great. I just can’t seem to make myself pick up right away.
Since the warehouse incident, have you noticed yourself feeling ongoing fear, anger, or guilt, especially when thinking about what happened or reminders of it?

I’m not sure. I mean, I get uncomfortable thinking about it, but I don’t know if I’d call it ongoing fear or anger or guilt exactly.

Guilt is a weird word, because then I start thinking, like, should I have noticed something during the inspection, but also that’s not really my job in the same way it would be for safety people, and then I start arguing with myself about job titles and responsibility and—sorry. I don’t know.

I guess I haven’t really noticed one clear feeling that stays around. It’s more like I don’t want to think about it too much.
Since the warehouse incident, have you found yourself feeling afraid, angry, or guilty most days, even when you're not directly thinking about the event?

I don’t know that I’d say most days. I mean… I’ve been more on edge in general, but “afraid, angry, or guilty” feels so specific, and I don’t always know what I’m feeling until later.

Like, sometimes I’ll be at work and someone will ask a totally normal question, and I’ll feel irritated, but then maybe that’s just because the copier was jammed again or because everyone sends emails with no subject line, which is its own crime, honestly. Sorry—that’s not really what you asked.

I guess I haven’t noticed one of those feelings being there most days when I’m not thinking about it. It’s more like I try not to check in with myself too much.
Since the warehouse incident, have you found yourself feeling numb, detached, or losing interest in activities you usually enjoy, even when you’re not thinking about the event?

I’m not sure. I don’t think I’ve noticed that exactly… like, numb or detached sounds pretty strong, and I don’t know if I’d use those words.

I mean, I still do normal things. I go through work, come home, make dinner if I remember I bought groceries before they turn into some kind of science project in the fridge. And activities I enjoy… I don’t know, I haven’t really checked whether I’m enjoying them less, if that makes sense. Sometimes I’m just tired, but that could be a hundred things.

So… I guess I wouldn’t say I’ve clearly been feeling numb or losing interest. Not that I’ve noticed.
Have you noticed any ongoing emotional reactions, like fear, anger, or guilt, even when you're not thinking about the warehouse incident?

I don’t think so, not in a clear way. I mean, I can get kind of… off, I guess, but if I’m not thinking about the warehouse thing, I don’t usually sit there feeling afraid or angry or guilty.

It’s hard because if you ask me to name an emotion, I start overthinking it, like those little mood tracker apps where they give you twelve versions of “bad” and I’m like, I don’t know, do I feel “uneasy” or “apprehensive,” and then I delete the app. So, no… I haven’t really noticed ongoing fear, anger, or guilt when it’s not on my mind.
Since the warehouse incident, have you found yourself getting easily irritated or angry, even during times when you’re not thinking about what happened?

Yeah… I think that one, maybe. I don’t feel angry all the time, but I’ve noticed I’m quicker to snap.

Like, there was this junior analyst at work who asked me a pretty small question about a spreadsheet—honestly, the kind of thing I’ve asked people before—and I answered way harsher than I meant to. It wasn’t even a big deal, it was just… a formula or a column thing, I don’t remember exactly. And then afterward I felt really embarrassed, because that’s not how I usually talk to people.

I mean, spreadsheets are annoying on a normal day too, so it’s hard to know what’s what. But yeah, I guess I have been more irritable than usual.
Since the warehouse incident, have you found yourself taking less interest in things you used to care about or enjoy, even outside of work?

I don’t know… I mean, maybe a little, but I haven’t really been tracking it that way.

Like, outside of work I usually… well, I used to do this pottery class thing sometimes, not that I was good at it—everything I made looked like a bowl that got sad halfway through—but I haven’t gone in a bit. But that might just be because scheduling is annoying, and the studio changed their sign-up system and it’s one of those websites that makes you want to throw your laptop into a pond.

So I’m not sure I’d say I’ve lost interest. I still care about things, I think. I just… haven’t really noticed a clear change like that.
Since the warehouse incident, have you found yourself feeling afraid, angry, or guilty most days, even when you're not directly thinking about the event?

I’m not sure I’d say “most days,” no. I mean, I have bad moments, and sometimes I’m just… kind of short with people, like I said. But if I’m not thinking about the warehouse, I don’t usually notice myself sitting there feeling afraid or guilty or anything specific like that.

Angry is tricky because, I mean, everyone gets annoyed—like my building’s laundry room has this machine that eats quarters, which shouldn’t even be possible anymore, it’s 2026, but somehow here we are. So I can get irritated. But I don’t know that it’s this constant feeling most days. I haven’t really noticed it that clearly.
Since the warehouse incident, have you found yourself feeling afraid, angry, or guilty most days, even when you're not directly thinking about the event?

I think I kind of answered this, but… no, I don’t think it’s most days. Or at least I haven’t been walking around thinking, “Oh, I’m scared,” or “I feel guilty,” if that makes sense.

I do get annoyed more easily sometimes, but then I’ll be like—well, maybe anyone would be annoyed, because the printer at work jams every single time you need something fast, and somehow it always says “tray two empty” when tray two is absolutely not empty. Sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

I guess the short answer is: I haven’t noticed those feelings being there most days when I’m not thinking about the warehouse.
Since the warehouse incident, have you found yourself feeling afraid, angry, or guilty most days, even when you're not directly thinking about the event?

Yeah, I know, I’m sorry, I think I keep circling this one. I don’t really have a better answer than… I haven’t noticed that, not in a steady “most days” kind of way.

Like, I’ll have moments where I’m tense or irritated, but then it’s hard to tell if that’s because of the warehouse thing or because, I don’t know, my email inbox has become some kind of living organism. But if I’m not thinking about what happened, I don’t usually register fear or guilt or anger as this background thing. At least not that I can clearly point to.
Since the warehouse incident, have you found yourself feeling afraid, angry, or guilty on most days, even when you're not thinking about the event?

I guess I’m still kind of not sure how to answer that in the exact way you’re asking. Like, “most days” feels like a lot, and I haven’t really been tracking it.

I can get irritated, definitely, but then I start thinking about whether that’s just normal life stuff—like my upstairs neighbor has apparently decided 11 p.m. is a great time to rearrange furniture, which would make anyone annoyed, right? But afraid or guilty when I’m not thinking about the warehouse… I don’t really notice that as a regular thing.

So, no, I don’t think I can say that’s happening most days.
Since the warehouse incident, have you found it difficult to experience positive emotions like happiness, satisfaction, or loving feelings, even in moments that used to bring you joy?

Um… I don’t know. I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed that exactly. Like, I can still enjoy things, I think. Maybe not always in the same way, but I don’t know if that’s because of what happened or because I’m tired or distracted or whatever.

Like, I watched this dumb cooking show the other night—one of those ones where everyone acts like undercooked risotto is a personal betrayal—and I did laugh at that. So I don’t think I’m completely unable to feel good things.

I guess… no, I haven’t really noticed a clear problem with feeling happiness or satisfaction or love. Not something I can point to and say, “Yes, that’s happening.”
Since the warehouse incident, have you found yourself feeling afraid, angry, or guilty on most days, even when you're not thinking about the event?

Right, sorry, I feel like you asked that already and I’m still giving you a messy answer.

I don’t think so. Not “most days” when I’m not thinking about it. I mean, I get annoyed or on edge sometimes, but then I’m like—well, everyone gets annoyed, especially when work is being ridiculous and someone sends a spreadsheet with twelve tabs and no explanation.

But afraid, angry, or guilty just sitting there in the background when I’m not thinking about the warehouse… I haven’t really noticed that. At least not in a way I could honestly say yes to.
Since the warehouse incident, have you found yourself feeling afraid, angry, or guilty on most days, even when you're not thinking about the event?

I’m sorry, I know we’re circling this one. I still don’t think I can say yes to that.

Like, I have moods, obviously—yesterday I got weirdly mad at the printer at work because it kept claiming there was no paper when there was clearly paper, which felt very personal in the moment. But that’s not really what you’re asking, I don’t think.

Afraid or guilty or angry just… hanging around most days when I’m not thinking about the warehouse? I haven’t noticed that. I’m not saying I’m perfectly calm all the time, but I don’t think it’s most days in the way you mean.
Since the warehouse incident, have you found it difficult to experience positive emotions like happiness, satisfaction, or loving feelings, even in moments that used to bring you joy?

I mean… I don’t think so. Or at least I haven’t noticed it in that specific way.

Like, I still have moments where something feels nice. I had coffee with my friend last weekend and we were talking about this horrible apartment she looked at—apparently the bathroom door didn’t fully open because it hit the toilet, which is… I don’t even know how that passes as a floor plan—and I did laugh. I remember feeling like, okay, that was actually funny.

So, no, I wouldn’t say I can’t feel happiness or satisfaction or anything like that. Maybe I’m a little more distracted sometimes, but I don’t think I’ve lost those feelings.
Since the warehouse incident, have you found yourself feeling down, hopeless, or having little interest in doing things most days, even when you’re not thinking about the event?

Um… I’m not sure I’d put it that way. I have definitely had days where I’m kind of blah and don’t want to do much, but “most days” feels like a lot.

Like, I still do things. Maybe not enthusiastically every second, but I’ll watch something dumb or go get food, and I can still be interested once I’m doing it. The other night I got pulled into watching those videos where people restore old furniture, which is not something I ever planned to care about, and suddenly it was an hour later.

So… down or hopeless most days, when I’m not thinking about the warehouse? I don’t think I’ve noticed that. Maybe some low moments, but not like a constant thing.
